structured_output.world_model: W5 (contrarian), after E017. The key fact is E016→E017. Removing graph breaks should leave the math identical, yet accuracy fell 0.70 pp (0.7607→0.7537). The 3-seed mean therefore reshuffles by about ±0.35 pp (1σ), not ±0.15. E016's +0.33 pp from halving weight decay is indistinguishable from reshuffle noise. The keep rule has been selecting lucky draws (E015, E016), so I put the true mean of the tip recipe at about 0.755–0.756. The tip's 0.07 pp margin is a lottery ticket, not a resource. Every trim (epochs, pixels, width, depth) costs at least 0.3 pp in expectation and will mostly come in below 0.753 on 3 seeds. The loop needs a real accuracy booster of at least 0.5 pp, verified on many seeds, before any trim can stick. Code facts: Muon applies no weight decay and renormalizes the filters, so filter weight decay is inert. The run is 9.5 true epochs, and Newton-Schulz already uses 3 steps. Time follows FLOPs and pixels: per-step pixel cost 24:28:32 px = 0.56:0.77:1. Conv multiply-accumulates are about 21/51/28% for groups 1/2/3, and group 1's third conv is about 7%. A mechanism to check: if keeping the LR as a GPU tensor or capturing graphs changed RNG consumption or captured the LR stale, E017's drop is real rather than noise. A diff of the per-step LR trace between E016 and E017 would settle it.

forecasts.reason: About 8% fewer pixels, but the abrupt 24→32 px jump likely costs 0.3-0.5 pp, which 3 seeds cannot separate from ±0.35 pp of reshuffle noise.
E017's 0.7 pp drop with identical math implies E016 was drawn high; I expect a 10-seed mean of about 0.755-0.756, below 0.757.
About -10% time for -0.5 to -0.8 pp against a true margin near zero.
Group 2 is the capacity core and its width also feeds group 3; the loss likely exceeds 0.25 pp.
Filter weight decay is inert; a head-temperature effect of about 0.1 pp at most is buried in ±0.35 pp of 3-seed noise.
That conv is about 7% of FLOPs plus memory traffic, so about -6.5% time, short of 8%, and losing depth at the highest resolution costs accuracy.
Swapping 15% of steps from 24 px to 20 px saves only about 3% of time, below the 4% threshold; the loss is mild, but the margin is about zero.

cruxes: Was E017's 0.70 pp drop pure reshuffle noise, or did graph-break removal change the math (stale LR captured in a CUDA graph, changed RNG consumption)? Diff the per-step LR and the RNG trace between E016 and E017.
What is the 10-seed held-out mean of the tip: about 0.756 (trims are hopeless without a booster) or 0.759 or more (about 0.5 epoch can be trimmed)?

Is there any accuracy booster worth at least 0.5 pp at near-zero time (BN recalibration at 32 px, longer 32 px tail with a shorter total, a head-only weight decay or temperature change) that holds up on 10 seeds?
